claims.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
claims.evidence: A shortest cycle surviving in G-S is chordless and hence induced; bipartiteness makes its length even, while an induced cycle of length at least 10 contains an induced P8 on eight consecutive vertices. Thus only C4, C6, and C8 need be hit. When S is an FVS, every remaining component is a tree; P8-freeness bounds its diameter by 6 and therefore its radius by 3. Inclusion-minimality makes restoring each x create a cycle through x, whose deletion leaves a path between two distinct neighbors of x in one remaining component.
claims.witness: The shortest-surviving-cycle and restored-vertex arguments form direct certificates for all three assertions.
claims.search_method: Independent deductive reconstruction from the definitions; no web or other evidence files used.

claims.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
claims.evidence: The induced C4/C6/C8 list is a rank-at-most-eight hypergraph whose transversals are exactly the FVSs by claim 0. Branching on every vertex of an unhit edge has depth k and at most O(8^k) nodes; scanning the O(n^8) obstruction list at each node gives the stated bound. For approximation, the union U of a maximal vertex-disjoint obstruction packing hits every obstruction. If the packing has p members, OPT is at least p and |U| is at most 8p, proving the factor 8.
claims.witness: The bounded-search tree and maximal-packing inequalities OPT≥p and |U|≤8p are complete certificates.
claims.search_method: Direct algorithm and approximation-ratio analysis from the verified obstruction equivalence.

claims.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
claims.evidence: Independent exhaustive extension of a fixed ordered simple path reproduced the survivor counts 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 for orders 1 through 15. At every extension all parity-permitted chords were considered, and graphs were rejected exactly for a C4 or induced P8; hence no admissible graph has a 15-vertex simple path. In an undirected DFS every edge joins ancestor-comparable vertices. Bags consisting of each vertex and all its DFS ancestors have size at most 14, cover every edge, and satisfy running intersection, so their width is at most 13. Standard finite connectivity states then give polynomial-time FVS.
claims.witness: The exhaustive certificate terminates with zero admissible ordered Hamilton-path supergraphs on 15 vertices.
claims.search_method: Independent exact enumeration plus a direct verification of the DFS tree-decomposition axioms.

claims.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
claims.evidence: Four-way branching on an uncovered C4, with iterative deepening, finds a minimum C4-transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. Claim 2 supplies a width-13 decomposition of G-X. Adding X to every bag gives width at most r+13 and covers edges incident with or internal to X. A nice-decomposition FVS DP recording deleted boundary vertices and the connectivity partition of retained boundary vertices has 2^{O(r log r)} states; edge and join transitions reject exactly cycle-closing combinations. The product bound stated in the claim is therefore valid.
claims.witness: A minimum C4-transversal X is the parameter certificate; the augmented decomposition has bags of size at most r+14.
claims.search_method: Independent parameterized-runtime and tree-decomposition analysis, including the r=0 boundary case.

claims.claim: On a chain graph—one whose neighborhoods on a bipartition side are linearly ordered by inclusion—a maximum-gain induced forest for arbitrary rational vertex gains, with one specified vertex optionally forced retained or deleted, is constructible in O(n^2). Consequently, weighted Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on chain graphs, including half-graphs with unbounded C4-transversal number.
claims.evidence: For any retained subsets of a Ferrers-ordered chain graph, the induced graph is a forest exactly when at most one retained A-vertex has two retained B-neighbors: a cycle supplies two such A-vertices, while nesting makes any two such vertices share two B-neighbors and form a C4. Conditioning on the second selected B-position q therefore leaves exactly the independent choices and single high-A choice appearing in the draft's formula. The cases with at most one B plus all q cover every feasible set. Deletion is handled by removing the specified vertex; a bonus exceeding twice the total absolute gain forces retention without changing the relative order of retained solutions. Exhaustive small exact tests with signed fractional gains agreed with the formula and forcing reductions.
claims.witness: The forest characterization reduces every feasible solution uniquely to either the at-most-one-B case or a second-B index q.
claims.search_method: Symbolic case analysis supplemented by exhaustive integer-bitmask and Fraction checks.

claims.claim: Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on graphs whose every block is a chain graph. This gives a direct exact algorithm for a P8-free subclass that can contain both C4 and an induced P7.
claims.evidence: Every cycle is contained in one block, so global forest feasibility is equivalent to forest feasibility in every retained block. Rooting the block-cut forest and conditioning each articulation on retained/deleted separates its descendant subproblems. Each pair of child values becomes a constant plus an arbitrary unary gain at the articulation, exactly matching claim 4's forced-state chain oracle; assigning each original vertex cost once avoids double counting. The displayed eight-vertex example contains a C4 and the asserted chordless P7, has only chain blocks, and cannot induce P8 because its entire eight-vertex graph contains the extra C4 edges.
claims.witness: The block-cut forest supplies the two-state decomposition; the stated C4 with two length-two pendant paths is an explicit boundary member.
claims.search_method: Direct block-decomposition proof and manual adjacency check of the eight-vertex example.

claims.claim: For every n≥2, the half-graph H_n is P5-free and has no false twins, yet its minimum C4-transversal has size n-2 and its treewidth is at least ⌈n/2⌉. Thus neither bounded C4-transversal number nor bounded treewidth follows from P8-freeness, even after excluding false twins.
claims.evidence: The two neighborhood chains are strict and nonempty, proving absence of false twins. Chain graphs are induced-2K2-free, whereas every induced P5 contains an induced 2K2. If a C4-free retained set has second-smallest retained A-index j, it has at most n-j+2 A-vertices and at most j B-vertices, hence at most n+2 vertices; all B together with a_{n-1},a_n attains n+2, yielding transversal size n-2. With p=⌈n/2⌉, the specified vertices contain K_{p,p}; contracting p-1 matching edges produces a K_{p+1} minor, so treewidth is at least p. Exact enumeration confirmed the finite formulas through n=8.
claims.witness: The family H_n itself witnesses both unbounded quantities while remaining P5-free and false-twin-free.
claims.search_method: General symbolic counting and minor construction, supplemented by exhaustive exact checks for n=2 through 8.

claims.claim: There are 2-connected C4-free P8-free bipartite graphs of unbounded order: the graph formed by m≥2 internally disjoint length-three paths between two common terminals has 2m+2 vertices.
claims.evidence: Every simple cycle consists of two complete arms and has length six, so no C4 occurs. Deleting either terminal leaves a connected subdivided star; deleting an internal vertex leaves the terminals connected through another intact arm, so there is no cut vertex. An induced path avoiding both terminals has at most two vertices, one containing exactly one terminal has at most five, and one containing both has one full arm plus at most one extra internal vertex beyond each terminal, hence at most six. Thus the family is P8-free and has unbounded order 2m+2. Exact enumeration confirmed these properties for m=2 through 7.
claims.witness: The length-three multi-arm theta graph for each m≥2 is the explicit infinite family.
claims.search_method: Symbolic cycle, cut-vertex, and induced-path case analysis with finite exact checks at small m.

claims.claim: The natural LP that assigns nonnegative vertex weights and requires total weight at least one on every induced C4, C6, and C8 has integrality gap at least 2-o(1) on P8-free bipartite graphs: on K_{n,n} its exact fractional optimum is n/2 while its FVS optimum is n-1.
claims.evidence: K_{n,n} is P4-free and its only induced cycles are C4s. A retained subgraph is acyclic exactly when at least one side has at most one retained vertex, so the maximum retained order is n+1 and the FVS optimum is n-1. There are binom(n,2)^2 C4 constraints and each vertex belongs to (n-1)binom(n,2) of them. Summing the constraints gives objective at least n/2, while uniform value 1/4 is feasible. Hence the exact ratio is 2-2/n. Fraction-based enumeration confirmed all counts and optima for n=2 through 7.
claims.witness: The family K_{n,n} witnesses ratios 2-2/n tending to 2.
claims.search_method: Exact symbolic incidence counting and Fraction-based finite verification.

target_evidence: The exact source target requires a polynomial-time algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on every P8-free bipartite graph. The draft explicitly states that it does not establish this and proves only an exponential-in-k algorithm, an approximation, parameterized tractability, and polynomial algorithms for proper subclasses. Those are correct and material partial results, but none yields polynomial time on the entire target class. Therefore the draft's PARTIAL resolution label is accurate.
